turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Good afternoon, I am Sister Meena. Let me take the readings quickly. Blood pressure one twenty-eight over eighty-two, pulse eighty-eight, temperature thirty-seven point one, oxygen ninety-seven percent, breathing eighteen a minute. Doctor is free, you can go in.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): Come, sit. I am Dr. Iyer. What brings you today?
[SEG0003] person_3 (PATIENT): The cough, doctor. After the flu it started and it is still there, six weeks now. At night it gets much worse, and I cannot sleep properly.
[SEG0004] person_2 (DOCTOR): Six weeks is a long stretch. Did that flu come with fever and body ache, or only a cold?
[SEG0005] person_3 (PATIENT): Fever was there for four days, whole body was paining. Then the fever went and the cough stayed. My wife was telling me to come earlier, I thought it would settle only.
[SEG0006] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any blood in the phlegm? Or pain in the chest when you—

[SEG0007] person_3 (PATIENT): Phlegm is white, mostly in the morning, no blood, and at night it is dry and just goes on. Is cold water bad, because I drink straight from the fridge? Sorry, you asked something else also.
[SEG0008] person_2 (DOCTOR): Leave the cold water for now. I was asking about chest pain, and if you get breathless when you walk.
[SEG0009] person_3 (PATIENT): Chest pain, no. Two floors up to the flat, I feel a little tight. My work is accounts, sitting only most of the day, so otherwise I don't notice.
[SEG0010] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any weight loss? Fever now? Night sweats?

[SEG0011] person_3 (PATIENT): Weight loss, no. I eat the same rice and dal. Fever is not there now. Night sweats, I don't think so, not the drenching kind. The cough wakes me and I feel a bit warm, that is all.
[SEG0012] person_2 (DOCTOR): Have you travelled recently, or been in contact with tuberculosis?
[SEG0013] person_3 (PATIENT): Travel, no. I have not left Pune since last year. TB contact also no, nobody at home. Should I wear a mask in the office? People are looking when I cough.
[SEG0014] person_2 (DOCTOR): Mask, after I examine you, not before. What regular medicines are you on, and any drug allergy?

[SEG0015] person_3 (PATIENT): Amlodipine five mg in the morning for BP, since three years. I don't miss it. For the cough I took Ascoril, two spoons at night, but I stopped last week, too much drowsiness at work. Allergy, no, nothing.
[SEG0016] person_2 (DOCTOR): So amlodipine five milligrams every morning stays, and Ascoril is stopped. Shirt up, please, and deep breaths—
[SEG0017] person_3 (PATIENT): Is this TB, doctor? My neighbour's night cough was TB. The grandchildren come on Sundays, do I tell them not to come? I am really—
[SEG0018] person_2 (DOCTOR): I am not putting any name on this. Breathe in for me... once more... other side now.
[SEG0019] person_2 (DOCTOR): There are a few crackles at the right base. The left side is clear. No wheeze. Throat is a little red, nothing dramatic.
[SEG0020] person_3 (PATIENT): Crackles means infection, no? Will you give an antibiotic today? I cannot take more leave, my boss already—
[SEG0021] person_2 (DOCTOR): Not an antibiotic in the dark. Crackles mean some moisture or irritation, they don't name the cause. You said no weight loss, is that still right?

[SEG0022] person_3 (PATIENT): I said no. Well, actually, the trousers are loose. Belt was on the third hole, now it is the fifth. Maybe two or three kilos, I have no scale. Since when, I can't tell you.
[SEG0023] person_2 (DOCTOR): Loose clothes, I am not ignoring that. Diabetes, asthma, any old lung trouble?

[SEG0024] person_3 (PATIENT): Sugar was normal about six months back. Asthma, no. My father had a heart attack at sixty-two, that is all. I have never smoked, and on weekends I take one small peg of whisky, only one.
[SEG0025] person_2 (DOCTOR): Never smoked, one weekend peg, father had a heart attack. I need the contact question again, properly. Anyone in the extended family on tuberculosis treatment?
[SEG0026] person_3 (PATIENT): If you are sending me for an X-ray, can it be after six? I have to phone my boss, he is already upset about the—

[SEG0027] person_1 (NURSE): Sorry, doctor, his sister is just outside. She told me a cousin in Nagpur was started on tuberculosis tablets about two months ago, and that he had stayed in that house for a few days in March.
[SEG0028] person_3 (PATIENT): No, she is mixing it. I went for one evening only, a naming ceremony, I did not stay the night. Nobody said it was TB. She always stretches the story.

[SEG0029] person_2 (DOCTOR): I will let the six o'clock question go. On contact I have two stories, your one evening without being told, and your sister's few days with treatment, via the nurse. I cannot sort that here, and I am still not naming a cause.
[SEG0030] person_3 (PATIENT): Then what is in your mind, TB or not? I need something to tell the office, and something to tell the children. Please, straight.

[SEG0031] person_2 (DOCTOR): I am thinking aloud, not concluding. A cough after flu can drag on for weeks. Loose clothes plus this unclear exposure mean I look further before I use any disease name. The step is a chest X-ray, not a label.
[SEG0032] person_3 (PATIENT): Can they do it today? Is the radiation bad for me? Maybe five years ago I had a pre-employment chest X-ray, they said normal, I think. The report is not with me.
[SEG0033] person_2 (DOCTOR): One PA film is a small dose, not a CT. I am ordering a chest X-ray, PA view, today, downstairs.
[SEG0034] person_3 (PATIENT): Suppose the X-ray is normal, am I free? I read that TB can be there even with a normal film. After reading it I could not sleep.
[SEG0035] person_2 (DOCTOR): I am not taking that question today. If the film is abnormal, or if the cough has not settled, we may send a sputum test. Only in that case. Not today.
[SEG0036] person_1 (NURSE): Counter three has two thirty free. I will book the chest X-ray in that slot.
[SEG0037] person_3 (PATIENT): Two thirty works. What do I do for the night cough? Ascoril made me sleepy in office. Is there some milder syrup?

[SEG0038] person_2 (DOCTOR): No cough syrup until the film is seen. Steam two times, two extra pillows so you stay propped up, warm water with a little honey if the throat is tickling. Do not start Ascoril again.
[SEG0039] person_3 (PATIENT): Two times, morning and night? Honey, how many spoons? Mask at home for the children, yes or no? I even worry about one spoon, because of sugar. The mind doesn't stop.

[SEG0040] person_2 (DOCTOR): Steam in the morning and before bed. One spoon of honey in warm water, only to soothe, and that is alright when the sugar test was normal. Use a simple mask if you are coughing near the grandchildren. Precaution, not a diagnosis.
[SEG0041] person_3 (PATIENT): Sister, can you check weight today? The last number in my head is from before Diwali, or somewhere near it, I don't really remember. I don't trust the pharmacy scale.
[SEG0042] person_1 (NURSE): The clinic scale is outside. I can take it now, doctor, if you want.
[SEG0043] person_2 (DOCTOR): Yes, please do it before he goes downstairs. We missed the weight at the start.
[SEG0044] person_1 (NURSE): Sixty-eight point five kilograms. He has a phone note of seventy-one, but he cannot say which day he wrote it.
[SEG0045] person_3 (PATIENT): Maybe January. I don't know which year. So the weight has come down, and that frightens me. Is sixty-eight point five low? I am five foot eight.

[SEG0046] person_2 (DOCTOR): At five foot eight, sixty-eight point five is not a low weight. A change would matter, but there is no reliable previous number and no date, so I will not guess a speed. The X-ray is still first.
[SEG0047] person_3 (PATIENT): For the report, do I come back or will somebody phone? If I get more tight in the chest tonight, should I go to emergency? I know I am asking a lot.

[SEG0048] person_2 (DOCTOR): Come back in three days with the film. I will see you whether it is normal or not, that visit is fixed. If you are very breathless, or you cough blood, or a high fever starts, go to emergency the same day. Don't wait for the appointment.
[SEG0049] person_3 (PATIENT): And Ascoril, not even a smaller dose? Some nights I took one spoon only, not two, and some nights I left it. I was not regular at all.

[SEG0050] person_2 (DOCTOR): Don't restart it, whatever the spoon was. You were not taking it steadily, so it is not a course I can use. Amlodipine five milligrams every morning, continue that, don't miss it.

[SEG0051] person_3 (PATIENT): Amlodipine I never miss, that one I am strict. Six weeks I counted from the fever's first day. I think six is right. My sister might remember it as five, I never asked her, so—
[SEG0052] person_2 (DOCTOR): We stay with six weeks, because that is what you actually counted. I won't take a number that was never said. Any loose motions? Any burning when you pass urine?
[SEG0053] person_3 (PATIENT): What is worrying me more is the sentence for my boss. Please see the X-ray film yourself, not only some typed line. I don't want a wrong word going to the office.
[SEG0054] person_2 (DOCTOR): I will see the film myself, yes. Just the motions and the urine, so I can close that.
[SEG0055] person_3 (PATIENT): Motions are normal. Urine has no burning. No pain anywhere else. Only the cough and this worry.

[SEG0056] person_1 (NURSE): The form is ready. Counter three, two thirty, and you need not be fasting. I have written sixty-eight point five for the weight. OPD return is pencilled three days from today.

[SEG0057] person_2 (DOCTOR): If they cannot do the film today, call the OPD number on the form and we will shift the visit. If they do it, I see you in three days as planned. Try not to read more about this tonight.

features: patient_answers_other_question: the patient answers a different question than the one asked, and the doctor repeats or lets it go.
interruptions_trailing_off: people interrupt each other, trail off, or the answer comes two turns after the question.

bad.reason: Worry/anxiety is evident, but certainty 'certain' is stronger than transcript states.
Past pre-employment chest X-ray is mentioned, but not requested by patient.

omissions.text: Ascoril dose was two spoons at night for cough before stopping last week because it caused too much drowsiness at work; the recorded medication omits the dose and reason for stopping.

Tuberculosis contact history is incorrectly recorded as a family history of tuberculosis in a cousin. What was actually said is an unclear possible exposure: the nurse relayed that the patient's sister reported a cousin in Nagpur had started TB treatment two months ago and that the patient had stayed there for a few days in March, while the patient disputed this and said he went for one evening only and was not told it was TB.
Negative finding not recorded: no recent travel; patient had not left Pune since last year.
Negative finding not recorded: no known household tuberculosis contact ('nobody at home').
Negative finding not recorded: no diabetes / 'sugar was normal about six months back.'
Negative finding not recorded: no other old lung trouble.
Weight-loss detail not recorded: patient described trousers becoming loose, belt changing from the third hole to the fifth, estimated about 2-3 kg lost, but timing was unclear.
Pre-employment chest X-ray is recorded too definitively as completed; the patient only said maybe five years ago he had one and thought it was normal, and the report was not with him.
Follow-up detail not recorded: doctor said he would see the patient in three days whether the chest X-ray is normal or not, and would personally review the film.

omissions.text: Past flu illness details before the cough: fever for four days with generalized body aches, then fever resolved and cough persisted.
Current cough detail not recorded: the patient reports the cough wakes him at night and he cannot sleep properly.
Negative finding nuance: the patient denied current night sweats specifically saying not the drenching kind, but did say he sometimes feels a bit warm when awakened by cough.

Uncertain tuberculosis exposure history also included the patient's own statement that there was no known TB contact at home and nobody had told him the cousin had TB; this uncertainty was part of the discussion before the conflicting sister report.
Ascoril discontinuation reason and timing were not fully captured in medications: he stopped it last week because it caused too much drowsiness at work.
Previous testing history: the patient said sugar/diabetes test was normal about six months ago.
Past pulmonary history denied more broadly: he denied any old lung trouble.
Additional symptom negative finding: no pain anywhere else.
The doctor advised no antibiotic empirically at this visit ('not an antibiotic in the dark').
Conditional testing plan nuance: sputum test would be considered only if the chest X-ray is abnormal or if the cough has not settled, and specifically not today.
Chest X-ray scheduling contingency: patient does not need to be fasting for the X-ray.
